This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 10 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/cn/shenzhen/ZGSZ.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Model consensus and observational baselines for the region support this value, with historical August highs often clustering near 32–36°C. Unexpected convective development, localized sea-breeze effects, or minor station measurement variations could still produce a recorded high of 35°C or 37°C, though such deviations appear unlikely given current guidance.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Shanghai’s August 12 highest temperature centers on 29°C (41.5%) and 30°C (32.5%), with 28°C at 21.5%, reflecting a narrow range shaped by recent tropical cyclone activity.** Typhoon Dolphin, which made landfall in Zhejiang Province near Shanghai around August 9–10, has delivered heavy rainfall, strong winds, and persistent cloud cover across eastern China. These conditions reduce surface solar heating and promote evaporative cooling, capping daytime maxima below typical mid-August values near 32–35°C.

Official monitoring and model guidance highlight ongoing overcast skies and isolated thunderstorms on August 12, which limit afternoon temperature recovery even as the system weakens. The close spread between 29°C and 30°C outcomes captures remaining uncertainty in exact peak timing, boundary-layer moisture, and any residual steering influences on the decaying low-pressure area. Historical August climatology shows highs often exceed 30°C under clearer subtropical ridge conditions, but the recent storm’s thermodynamic effects have shifted consensus toward the lower end of the distribution.

Upcoming short-range model runs and local observations from the China Meteorological Administration will provide the next resolution-relevant updates before the market settles.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Trader sentiment for Istanbul's peak temperature on August 12 heavily favors 28°C (56.5% implied probability) because ensemble forecasts from major models place the daytime maximum near or slightly below the long-term August average of 27–29°C.** Typical Mediterranean summer conditions—high pressure, light northerly winds, and Black Sea/Marmara moderation—limit extreme heat, while daytime solar heating and low cloud cover support readings in the upper 20s Celsius. Recent model runs show limited variability, with 29°C (23.5%) as the main alternative under slightly stronger insolation or reduced marine influence. Lower probabilities for 30°C+ reflect the absence of heatwave signals or southerly flow in the latest guidance, whereas cooler outcomes remain possible only if unexpected cloud cover or stronger sea breezes develop. Official monitoring from Turkish meteorological sources and global numerical weather prediction centers will provide key updates over the next 48 hours as the date approaches.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus favors a narrow 32–33°C range for Karachi’s August 12 high because late-monsoon climatology and extended model guidance place daily maxima near the 31–33°C August average, with AccuWeather’s outlook showing limited day-to-day variance. High humidity, light Arabian Sea breezes, and patchy convective cloud cover typically cap afternoon peaks while suppressing stronger radiative heating; recent surface observations and ensemble runs indicate no heatwave signal or steering pattern that would push readings outside this band. Below-normal rainfall forecasts may allow slightly clearer skies, favoring the modest edge for 33°C over 32°C, yet any increase in monsoon moisture could hold the maximum at the lower end. Updated Pakistan Meteorological Department guidance and next model cycles will refine resolution criteria ahead of the 48-hour window.
